highlights: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen for fast agentic workflows, and Orchestrator in Google Antigravity dynamically switches between models such as Carbon and Hydrogen. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while consuming 24% less quota on average and completing 19% faster.
Anthropic released self-hosted Claude Managed Agents in private beta, letting teams run the harness, sandboxes, credentials, and session history inside their own cloud or on-premise.
Hugging Face released Granite 4.1 3B and 8B LLMON preview models, an LLM-native markup language for communicating structure and semantics to models.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen for rapid execution across agentic workflows, and is bringing Gemini 4 to Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity. Orchestrator in Google Antigravity dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session; on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it reached near-Carbon task success rates while consuming 24% less quota on average and completing 19% faster.

evidence.quote: Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.
While our frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon , excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows.

With Hydrogen, we’re also bringing Gemini 4 to everyone — for all tiers of Google AI Studio , the Gemini API, Gemini for business , the Gemini app , Google Search , and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity .
To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity .
Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session.
On Terminal-Bench 4.0 , Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster.

items.title: Anthropic offers self-hosted Claude Managed Agents in private beta
items.summary: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents runs the harness, sandboxes, credentials, and session history in your own cloud or on-premise, with model requests routed to Anthropic directly, a cloud provider such as Amazon Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry, or your own gateway. Developers still build agents with the same core APIs as the hosted Managed Agents service, and access is available in private beta through your Anthropic account team.

evidence.quote: Category Product updates Product Claude Platform, Claude Managed Agents Date November 12, 2026 Reading time 5 min Share Copy link Contents Run your agent control plane in your own environment Designed for agent security Get started Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is now available in private beta.
With self-hosted Managed Agents, every part of the service runs in your own cloud or on-premise, including the harness, sandboxes, credentials, and session history.
You operate the Managed Agents server, its database, and the workers where agents run their shell and file tools.
Model requests go where you choose, whether that's Anthropic directly, your cloud provider (Amazon Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry), or your own gateway.
Your developers still build agents with the same core APIs as the hosted Managed Agents service.
Get started Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is now available in private beta.
Contact your Anthropic account team to request access, or read the docs to learn more.

items.title: Apple studies the theoretical limits of language model alignment
items.summary: Apple's research characterizes the information-theoretic limits of KL-regularized alignment by deriving the maximum achievable expected reward gain for a fixed KL-divergence budget, governed by a Jeffreys divergence term. The work yields a practical estimator based on base model samples, shows that reward ensembling mitigates reward hacking, and finds that best-of-NNN approaches the theoretical limit while PPO and GRPO remain substantially suboptimal.

evidence.quote: We characterize the information-theoretic limits of KL-regularized alignment by deriving the maximum achievable expected reward gain for a fixed KL-divergence budget.
Our first result provides a closed-form expression for the optimal reward improvement, governed by a Jeffreys divergence term rather than the √ K L √KL √ K L used in prior analyses.
We further reformulate this expression as a covariance under the base model, yielding a practical estimator that predicts achievable alignment gains from base model samples alone.

We extend our analysis to the proxy reward setting, showing that the gap between ideal and proxy alignment ( reward hacking ) grows with the magnitude of reward error and when the KL penalty factor decreases.
We then prove that reward ensembling mitigates reward hacking, providing a theoretical justification for this technique used in practice.

Empirically, we compute the KL–reward Pareto frontier for two tasks for LMs, safety and summarization, and show that best-of- N N N closely approaches the theoretical limit, while PPO and GRPO remain substantially suboptimal.

items.title: Hugging Face ships Granite 4.1 LLMON preview models
items.summary: Hugging Face developed LLMON, an LLM-native markup language that marks semantically coherent components with meaningful tags and wraps them in reserved special-token delimiters, and released two experimental preview models derived from Granite 4.1 base models: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview. A companion GitHub repo includes a toolkit plus workflow and template examples, and the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models while showing much stronger resistance to prompt injection.

evidence.quote: To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models.
Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters.
Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM.

Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.

Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview .
We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.
LLMON practically eliminates the problem on this benchmark, avoiding 47% more attacks relative to the best frontier model that we tested, and 95% more than the best open-source model.
Across standard benchmark categories, the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models.
In short, if you’re experimenting with Granite 4.1 3B or 8B today, you can swap in the LLMON preview and should see comparable general performance with much stronger resistance to prompt injection.

items.title: Edge0 open-sources Edge0-145B for local inference
items.summary: Edge0 open-sourced Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B along with a unified inference framework and deployment tools, describing Edge0-145B as an on-device model with 145 billion parameters. A compatible laptop needs reported peak memory of 29GB, with decoding above 80 tokens/s, and roughly 10B of the 145B total parameters participate in computation on each inference step.

evidence.quote: Introducing Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer November 12, 2026 · 19 min read · Edge0 releases Today, we're open-sourcing Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B , together with our unified inference framework and deployment tools.
Edge0-145B is the world's first open-source on-device AI model with 145 billion parameters.
A 145B model runs locally on a compatible laptop, with reported peak memory of 29GB and decoding above 80 tokens/s.
29GB peak memory
80+ tokens/s decode
Architecture: share large matrices across sparse experts.
Each group of 64 experts shares two large matrices, while each expert retains a small set of parameters that captures its differences.
Of the model's 145B total parameters, only approximately 10B participate in computation on each inference step.

items.title: Praxis-1 releases a 27B video-and-action diffusion model
items.summary: Praxis-1 is a 27B-parameter mixture-of-experts diffusion transformer that predicts video and actions together and is available on GitHub, on Hugging Face with native LeRobot support, and in vLLM-Omni, with weights plus inference and fine-tuning code released under Apache 2.0. It supports full fine-tuning and LoRA across NVIDIA hardware from data center GPUs like H100 and B200 down to Jetson Thor on the robot.

items.title: BotPsy-0.8B targets on-device tool use and agentic tasks
items.summary: BotPsy-0.8B is a 0.8B-parameter model built on top of Qwen3.5-0.8B for function calling and agentic workflows on device, with BF16 weights in Hugging Face safetensors format and GGUF files for llama.cpp and the QVAC SDK. It roughly doubles the agentic capability of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Think on key benchmarks: BFCL v4 rises from 23.4 to 44.0, ACEBench from 30.1 to 58.7, and τ-bench from 23.2 to 51.5.

evidence.quote: BotPsy-0.8B is a 0.8B-parameter model designed for function calling and agentic workflows, built on top of Qwen3.5-0.8B and suitable for on-device deployment.

BotPsy is a "personal assistant" that uses tools to perform a variety of simple tasks for the user, in domains such as web search & research, travel & lifestyle, commerce & finance, business & customer operations, device & vehicle control, files & documents, calendar, and email & messaging.
BotPsy achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) tool-use and agentic performance for its size, outperforming every model of up to 1.2B parameters that we tested.
This repository holds the BF16 weights in Hugging Face safetensors format.
GGUF files (BF16, Q8_0 and Q4_K_M) for llama.cpp and the QVAC SDK are in qvac/BotPsy-0.8B-GGUFs .

Twice the performance of its base model: BotPsy roughly doubles the agentic capability of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Think on key benchmarks: BFCL v4 rises from 23.4 to 44.0, ACEBench from 30.1 to 58.7, and τ-bench from 23.2 to 51.5 (mean of the retail, telecom and banking subsets).

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.323 adds Code Mode and plugin version ranges
items.summary: Claude Code v2.1.323 adds an experimental opt-in Code Mode in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools, and an engines["claude-code"] field in plugin.json so plugins outside their stated Claude Code version range are not installed, updated or loaded. The release also adds a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds while hooks run long in claude -p and SDK sessions, plus fixes for /compact, settings.json edits, and Edit and Bash running out of memory on certain /proc files.

evidence.quote: Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization
Added engines["claude-code"] to plugin.json : plugins outside their stated Claude Code version range are not installed, updated or loaded, and install and update pick the newest version that fits
Added a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds while hooks run long in claude -p and SDK sessions, so a host such as Claude Desktop won't end the turn as hung (once it includes this version)
Fixed running /compact again, or after a command such as /context , summarizing away a message that Claude had not answered yet
Fixed a setting saved in a running session undoing a hand edit made to settings.json moments earlier; a settings file you delete during a session now stays deleted
Fixed Edit and Bash running out of memory on certain /proc files, and Edit hanging or running out of memory on devices and named pipes

items.title: Codex 0.168.0 adds workspace panes and provider selection
items.summary: Codex 0.168.0 lets you browse model providers under Sessions → Model providers and choose the default for new chats, and enables features.tui_workspace to view a side conversation beside the main chat with a draggable divider or leader z to zoom. It also supports attaching recordings with an audio-capable model, features.image_generation_animation for generating or editing animated GIFs, and tui.notification method = "osc777" terminal notifications.

evidence.quote: Browse model providers under Sessions → Model providers and choose the default for new chats.
Enable features.tui_workspace to view a side conversation beside the main chat.
Drag the divider to resize the panes or press leader z to zoom the focused pane.
Attach recordings when using an audio-capable model.
Enable features.image_generation_animation to generate or edit animated GIFs with optional frame count and timing controls.
The app-server reference covers listing model providers, creating custom gateways, and updating gateway, Bedrock, and GCP settings.

items.title: Hugging Face posts token pooling-aware training for embeddings
items.summary: Token pooling-aware training teaches an encoder to preserve important information when similar token vectors are merged, and a new HierarchicalTokenPooling layer groups similar token embeddings using Ward hierarchical clustering with a straight-through estimator. With pool_factor=4, a normally trained model retains 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10 with a 4x reduction in document vectors, while pooling-aware training raises that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget.

evidence.quote: Token pooling makes these representations smaller by merging similar token vectors.
Pooling-aware training teaches the encoder to preserve the information that matters when its vectors are merged, helping you retrieve better from the same storage budget.
With pool_factor=4 , my normally trained model retains 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10, with a 4x reduction in document vectors.
Token pooling-aware training raises that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget!
HierarchicalTokenPooling groups similar token embeddings using Ward hierarchical clustering .
During training, HierarchicalTokenPooling uses a straight-through estimator to pass gradients from pooled vectors back to their member tokens, without differentiating the cluster assignments.

items.title: Hugging Face publishes a fine-tuning guide for TRELLIS.2
items.summary: This guide provides fine-tuning scripts and containers to fine-tune TRELLIS.2, a 3D model, on your own assets, running both locally and on Hugging Face Jobs. The configuration adds LoRA adapters only to the sparse-structure flow DiT and the shape flow DiT while freezing the texture flow DiT, training approximately 9.3 million adapter parameters in total for both targeted DiTs on a subset of 188 shoes from the 1,030 objects in GSO.

evidence.quote: TLDR; In this blog, we provide fine-tuning scripts and containers to fine-tune TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D model on your 3D assets, that can run both locally and on Hugging Face Jobs.
If you are interested in fine-tuning, you can use our scripts with few arguments (assuming you updated your dataset to Hugging Face Hub) or tinker with them yourself with this repository .
We add LoRA adapters only to the sparse-structure flow DiT and the shape flow DiT.
We freeze the texture flow DiT to keep its current capabilities.
Our subset has 188 shoes from the 1,030 objects in GSO.
Our configuration trains approximately 9.3 million adapter parameters in total for both targeted DiTs.

items.title: TOME-Math turns textbooks into structured proof supervision
items.summary: TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence) converts 2,118 textbooks spanning core areas of university-level mathematics into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Fine-tuning on TOME-Math at full scale raises the unweighted mean score across held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model, and the authors will release the corpus.

evidence.quote: We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links,
dependency references, and source provenance.

At full scale, fine-tuning on TOME-Math raises the unweighted mean score across our held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model, while exceeding all three public instruction-data baselines evaluated in aggregate.

items.title: Reinforcement learning incentivizes LLM self-learning
items.summary: This work studies self-learning, where LLMs autonomously retrieve, study, and apply knowledge from long-form reference materials, and introduces a BookNavigator interface plus reinforcement learning with fine-grained rewards to support that process. The method raises Intern-S2-Preview-35B's overall proof accuracy from 51.5% to 79.5%, beats RL-trained textbook-free and fixed-retrieval baselines, and adds 1.7 and 2.3 percentage points over the base model on BrowseComp-Plus and CL-bench.

items.title: SteerDistill quantizes LLM agents with closed-loop teacher steering
items.summary: SteerDistill is a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student execution, producing locally verified behavioral corrections that are then internalized for unassisted inference. Across five agentic benchmarks and three models, it exceeds the strongest quantized baseline by 1.67--2.18 points in average score under W4A16 and stays within one point of BF16, and on τ^2-Bench it outperforms QeRL by 1.84 percentage points in success rate using 67% fewer training GPU hours.

evidence.quote: We introduce SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student execution.
This closed-loop teacher steering produces locally verified behavioral corrections .

We internalize these corrections by training the student without guidance to match the steered student's predictions at corrected turns and the full-precision teacher 's at other turns, enabling unassisted inference .
Across five agentic benchmarks and three models, SteerDistill exceeds the strongest quantized baseline by 1.67--2.18 points in average score under W4A16 and stays within one point of BF16 .
On τ^2-Bench , it outperforms QeRL by 1.84 percentage points in success rate using 67% fewer training GPU hours and produces shorter successful trajectories than the quantized baselines.

items.title: Evolving Infra adapts LLM serving to agent workloads
items.summary: Evolving Infra is an agent-adaptive serving framework that decouples compute allocation from key--value (KV) cache management, letting nodes switch between prefill and decode, with an online planner matching the PD split to workload composition and an agent-aware distributed KV manager guiding cache eviction and transfer. Across coding, math, and computer-use tasks with GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 on up to 256 GB300 GPUs, it reduces mean end-to-end request latency and P95 TTFT by up to 4.1x and 14x over Dynamo, NVIDIA's production framework.

evidence.quote: We present Evolving Infra, an agent-adaptive serving framework that adapts compute allocation to agent workloads and KV cache management to agent context management at runtime.
We decouple compute allocation from key--value (KV) cache management, allowing nodes to switch efficiently between prefill and decode.

Building on this design, an online planner matches the PD split to workload composition, while an agent-aware distributed KV manager guides cache eviction and transfer with signals from agent context management.

Across coding, math, and computer-use tasks with GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 on up to 256 GB300 GPUs, Evolving Infra reduces mean end-to-end request latency and P95 TTFT by up to 4.1x and 14x over Dynamo, NVIDIA's production framework.

items.title: SparseRead cuts token use for web-facing AI agents
items.summary: SparseRead is a reusable reading control layer that governs content admission without modifying the agent model, combining a Read Intent Protocol, Adaptive Reader Backends, and a Budgeted Read Gate with faithful full-view fallback. Across six models, including Claude Opus 5, and five scenarios, it reduces total tokens by up to 92.9% and wall time by up to 89.0% while preserving or improving task quality in 97% settings, and on Web deep-search tasks it cuts tokens by 31.0--43.0% and task completion time by 23.0--37.0%.

items.title: PISA routes prompts to models by cost and quality
items.summary: PISA is a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router that combines soft cluster memberships with model-specific predictors to estimate individual model capabilities, and PISA-E extends it to ensemble routing by jointly selecting ensemble composition and cardinality under an explicit cost--quality preference adjustable at inference time without retraining. Across four LLM routing benchmarks under in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions, PISA achieves the highest macro-average cost--performance hypervolume among the evaluated single-model routers, while PISA-E surpasses the strongest ensemble competitors by 2.09 and 2.87 percentage points under ID and OOD conditions.

evidence.quote: We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router , and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing .
At the core of both methods, PISA combines soft cluster memberships with model-specific predictors to estimate individual model capabilities.
Building on these estimates, PISA-E jointly selects ensemble composition and cardinality under an explicit cost--quality preference that can be adjusted at inference time without retraining.

Across four LLM routing benchmarks under in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions, PISA achieves the highest macro-average cost--performance hypervolume among the evaluated single-model routers in both settings.

Meanwhile, PISA-E achieves the highest macro-average task performance among the evaluated ensemble approaches when prioritizing response quality, surpassing the strongest competitors by 2.09 and 2.87 percentage points under ID and OOD conditions, respectively.

items.title: Interactive Visual Gym benchmarks visual interaction models
items.summary: Interactive Visual Gym is a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users, instantiated as IVG-Bench with 315 interaction scenarios across cooking, household manipulation, and mobile-interface domains. The best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, completes only 53.4% of tasks within the time limit, and a human study finds 78.5% agreement between the interaction-quality metric and participant preferences.

evidence.quote: We introduce Interactive Visual Gym, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users.
We instantiate the framework as IVG-Bench , a benchmark with 315 interaction scenarios.

Evaluating state-of-the-art VLMs as visual interaction models reveals substantial limitations: the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, completes only 53.4% of tasks within the time limit, exhibits significant weaknesses in factual grounding and actionable guidance , and is often too slow to preve
We verify our evaluation protocol with a human study which finds 78.5% agreement between our interaction-quality metric and participant preferences.
